results.symptom: Intermittent ping loss and session drops. Pinging 192.168.1.10 results in mixed success (!) and timeout (.) messages. Switch MAC address table is rapidly reassigning ports (flapping).
results.expected_fault: Duplicate IP address conflict. IP 192.168.1.10 is statically assigned to two different active endpoints in the same broadcast domain.

rule_findings.fault: Duplicate IP address conflict involving 192.168.1.10.
rule_findings.evidence: Cisco reports a duplicate address for 192.168.1.10.
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Expected fault contains the rule's defining concepts.

results.symptom: CDP throws native VLAN mismatch syslog errors continuously. Potential untagged traffic leakage between broadcast domains.
results.expected_fault: Switch port native VLAN mismatch. Switch A is expecting untagged traffic on VLAN 10, while Switch B is using VLAN 20.

rule_findings.fault: Switch port native VLAN mismatch.
rule_findings.evidence: CDP reports a native VLAN mismatch: VLAN 20 versus VLAN 10.
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Expected fault contains the rule's defining concepts.

results.symptom: User lost network connection after replacing their computer. Switch port link status is physically down (red).
results.expected_fault: Port security maximum violation. An unauthorized MAC address attempted to transmit on a locked-down port, forcing it into an err-disabled shutdown state.

rule_findings.fault: Port security maximum violation caused the port to enter an err-disabled/shutdown state.
rule_findings.evidence: Port status is Secure-shutdown and Security Violation Count is 1.
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Expected fault contains the rule's defining concepts.

results.symptom: End hosts in VLAN 10 cannot reach their default gateway or other subnets. Ping to gateway 192.168.10.1 times out.
results.expected_fault: Router-on-a-Stick sub-interface VLAN tag mismatch. Sub-interface G0/0/0.10 is incorrectly configured with 802.1Q encapsulation for VLAN 20 instead of matching the access VLAN 10.

rule_findings.fault: Router-on-a-Stick sub-interface VLAN tag mismatch. Sub-interface g0/0/0.10 uses VLAN 20 instead of VLAN 10.
rule_findings.evidence: Interface suffix indicates VLAN 10, but encapsulation dot1Q uses VLAN 20.
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Semantic rule/evidence match.

results.symptom: All sub-interfaces remain in down/down status; complete loss of inter-VLAN routing across the network.
results.expected_fault: Router-on-a-Stick physical interface admin down. The parent interface (G0/0/0) was never brought online with the 'no shutdown' command, forcing all dependent sub-interfaces down.

rule_findings.fault: Parent interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0 is administratively down, causing dependent sub-interfaces to remain down.
rule_findings.evidence: GigabitEthernet0/0/0 is administratively down and 3 dependent sub-interface(s) are also down.
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Expected fault contains the rule's defining concepts.

results.symptom: The Port-Channel bundle fails to negotiate; ports operate independently and may cause spanning tree loops.
results.expected_fault: EtherChannel Protocol / Mode Mismatch. Switch A is attempting LACP (active) while Switch B is attempting PAgP (desirable).

rule_findings.fault: EtherChannel protocol/mode mismatch is preventing the port-channel from forming.
rule_findings.evidence: show etherchannel summary reports LACP while member ports remain stand-alone (I), and the symptom states that the bundle fails to negotiate.
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Semantic rule/evidence match.

results.symptom: Port-Channel fails consistency checks, placing member ports in a suspended or unbundled state.
results.expected_fault: EtherChannel Mismatched Allowed Trunk VLANs. Member ports of the same port-channel have conflicting allowed VLAN lists (VLAN 10,20 vs VLAN 10,30), causing the bundle to fail consistency checks.

rule_findings.fault: EtherChannel member ports have mismatched allowed VLAN lists.
rule_findings.evidence: fa0/1: VLANs 10,20, fa0/2: VLANs 10,30
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Expected fault contains the rule's defining concepts.

results.symptom: PC0 fails to obtain a DHCP lease and remains with IPv4 address 0.0.0.0, subnet mask 0.0.0.0 and default gateway 0.0.0.0.
results.expected_fault: DHCP relay agent is missing on Router1 G0/0.10; ip helper-address 192.168.20.10 is not configured.

rule_findings.fault: DHCP relay agent is missing on GigabitEthernet0/0.10; no ip helper-address is configured.
rule_findings.evidence: DHCP failure evidence is present and GigabitEthernet0/0.10 has no ip helper-address in the supplied configuration.
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Semantic rule/evidence match.

results.symptom: STP is operating on a redundant three-switch topology, but an inter-switch trunk has PortFast enabled, creating a risk of temporary Layer-2 loops, broadcast storms, and MAC flapping during topology changes.
results.expected_fault: PortFast was incorrectly enabled on Switch0 Fa0/1, which is an inter-switch trunk connected to Switch1 Fa0/1.

rule_findings.fault: PortFast is incorrectly enabled on an inter-switch trunk.
rule_findings.evidence: The interface is operating as a trunk while the spanning-tree output reports PortFast mode.
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Expected fault identifies PortFast on the inter-switch trunk.

results.symptom: PC0 cannot reach PC1 at 192.168.20.10 and ping fails with Request timed out or Destination host unreachable.
results.expected_fault: Static route on Router0 uses incorrect next-hop IP 10.1.1.5 instead of the actual adjacent Router1 IP 10.1.1.2.

rule_findings.fault: Static route to 192.168.20.0/24 uses an invalid next-hop address 10.1.1.5.
rule_findings.evidence: Configured next hop 10.1.1.5 does not belong to the directly connected network(s): 10.1.1.0/30.
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Expected fault contains the rule's defining concepts.

results.symptom: PC0 cannot successfully communicate with PC1 at 192.168.20.10; ICMP requests time out because the return path is missing.
results.expected_fault: Router1 is missing the reverse static route to 192.168.10.0/24 via Router0 at 10.1.1.1.

rule_findings.fault: Reverse route to the remote 192.168.10.0/24 network is missing from Router1.
rule_findings.evidence: Router1 fails to ping the remote host and its supplied routing table contains no route to 192.168.10.0/24.
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Semantic rule/evidence match.

results.symptom: Router0 treats the intended backup static route as equally preferred because both static routes have the same administrative distance of 1.
results.expected_fault: Backup static route was configured with AD 1 instead of a higher AD such as 10, so it is not functioning as a floating backup route.

rule_findings.fault: Multiple static routes to 192.168.20.0/24 have the same administrative distance.
rule_findings.evidence: All detected static routes use AD 1; a backup route should use a higher AD than the primary route.
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Semantic rule/evidence match.

results.symptom: OSPF neighbor adjacency between Router0 and Router1 fails or drops after the Hello timer is changed on one side.
results.expected_fault: OSPF Hello interval mismatch between Router0 and Router1. Router0 is configured with Hello 5 seconds while Router1 uses the default 10 seconds.

rule_findings.fault: OSPF Hello interval is configured as 5 seconds instead of the default 10 seconds.
rule_findings.evidence: show ip ospf interface reports Hello 5.
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Expected fault contains the rule's defining concepts.

results.symptom: OSPF neighbor adjacency between Router0 and Router1 fails to form or drops after the OSPF area is changed on one side.
results.expected_fault: OSPF area ID mismatch: Router0 is configured for Area 0 while Router1 is configured for Area 1 on the same transit link.

rule_findings.fault: OSPF area ID mismatch between neighboring interfaces.
rule_findings.evidence: Detected different OSPF areas: 0, 1.
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Expected fault contains the rule's defining concepts.

results.symptom: Hello packets are suppressed on the transit link; OSPF neighbor adjacency never establishes.
results.expected_fault: passive-interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0 was issued under the OSPF process on a transit link.

rule_findings.fault: OSPF passive-interface is enabled on a transit link.
rule_findings.evidence: The OSPF interface output explicitly reports 'No Hellos (Passive interface)'.
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Expected fault contains the rule's defining concepts.

results.symptom: Ingress WAN traffic gets filtered unintentionally while the target outbound host traffic remains unblocked.
results.expected_fault: Standard ACL applied in the wrong direction (ip access-group 10 in) on the egress WAN interface.

rule_findings.fault: Standard ACL is applied inbound on the inspected interface; for the supplied WAN scenario this is the wrong direction.
rule_findings.evidence: Interface shows inbound ACL 10, and ACL 10 is a standard IP ACL.
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Expected fault contains the rule's defining concepts.

results.symptom: Internal hosts can perform ping tests, but web pages fail to load because return TCP packets are blocked.
results.expected_fault: Extended ACL on WAN permits ICMP but is missing the "permit tcp any any established" rule.

rule_findings.fault: Extended ACL permits ICMP but lacks a permit for established TCP traffic.
rule_findings.evidence: ACL contains an ICMP permit but no 'permit tcp ... established' rule.
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Expected fault contains the rule's defining concepts.

results.symptom: Clients lose IP address leases or cannot resolve hostnames, despite direct IP reachability being active.
results.expected_fault: Extended ACL implicitly denies UDP, lacking explicit permits for UDP 53 and UDP 67/68.

rule_findings.fault: Extended ACL does not explicitly permit required DNS/DHCP UDP traffic.
rule_findings.evidence: Missing explicit permit(s): DNS/UDP 53, DHCP/UDP 67/68.
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Expected fault identifies the missing DNS/DHCP UDP permits.

results.symptom: Internal private IP packets pass to the Internet without translation; the upstream ISP drops them.
results.expected_fault: Omitted the ip nat inside command on the LAN gateway interface.

rule_findings.fault: LAN interface is missing the 'ip nat inside' configuration.
rule_findings.evidence: LAN interface reports NAT disabled while the WAN interface is configured as NAT outside.
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Expected fault contains the rule's defining concepts.

results.symptom: LAN devices have a valid default gateway but cannot access external networks; translations table is empty.
results.expected_fault: NAT ACL matches the wrong subnet (192.168.1.0 instead of 192.168.2.0).

rule_findings.fault: NAT ACL matches 192.168.1.0/24, but the detected inside LAN address is outside that subnet.
rule_findings.evidence: ACL permits 192.168.1.0/24; detected LAN address(es): 192.168.2.1.
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Semantic rule/evidence match.

results.symptom: External Internet users cannot reach the internal server via its public IP address.
results.expected_fault: 1-to-1 static NAT statement configured with inverted IP parameters (Public IP listed first).

rule_findings.fault: Static NAT mapping appears to have the public and private IP parameters inverted.
rule_findings.evidence: Inside global is 192.168.1.50 while inside local is 203.0.113.10.
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Expected fault contains the rule's defining concepts.

results.symptom: PC0 obtains an IP address via DHCP and can ping the default gateway and external public IPs (e.g., 8.8.8.8), but cannot browse websites using domain names (e.g., www.example.com).
results.expected_fault: DHCP server is advertising an incorrect or unreachable DNS server address (192.168.10.254) in its DHCP pool configuration.

rule_findings.fault: DHCP server is advertising an incorrect or unreachable DNS server address 192.168.10.254 in its DHCP pool configuration.
rule_findings.evidence: DNS server address 192.168.10.254 is configured in DHCP pool, but pinging it fails with 0% success.
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Expected fault contains the rule's defining concepts.

results.symptom: Switch0 is functioning normally and traffic flows between VLANs, but network administrators cannot telnet or SSH to the switch management IP (192.168.99.2) from another subnet.
results.expected_fault: Switch virtual interface (SVI) for the management VLAN (Vlan99) is administratively down (shutdown).

rule_findings.fault: Switch virtual interface (SVI) for the management VLAN (Vlan99) is administratively down (shutdown).
rule_findings.evidence: Interface Vlan99 is configured with IP 192.168.99.2 but status is administratively down.
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Expected fault contains the rule's defining concepts.

results.symptom: A host (PC0) in the sales department is connected to Switch port FastEthernet0/10. It cannot reach the sales gateway (192.168.10.1) or obtain a DHCP address. Pings to 192.168.10.1 fail.
results.expected_fault: Switch access port FastEthernet0/10 is assigned to the wrong VLAN (VLAN 20/Marketing) instead of Vlan 10/Sales.

rule_findings.fault: Switch access port fa0/10 is assigned to the wrong VLAN (VLAN 20) instead of the expected VLAN.
rule_findings.evidence: Interface fa0/10 is configured with access VLAN 20, which does not match the host's subnet.
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Expected fault contains the rule's defining concepts.

results.symptom: Router0 can ping its adjacent neighbors, but remote networks do not receive OSPF routes for the LAN network (192.168.10.0/24) connected to Router0's GigabitEthernet0/0/1 interface.
results.expected_fault: Router0's OSPF process configuration is missing the network statement for the LAN subnet (192.168.10.0/24), so this network is not being advertised.

rule_findings.fault: OSPF routing process configuration is missing the network statement for the local LAN subnet.
rule_findings.evidence: OSPF config contains neighbor network statements but lacks LAN subnet, and OSPF route table is empty.
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Expected fault contains the rule's defining concepts.

results.symptom: The first host on the LAN successfully connects to the Internet, but all subsequent hosts are unable to connect. Pings from host 2 to public IP addresses fail.
results.expected_fault: Dynamic NAT configuration is missing the 'overload' keyword at the end of the source mapping statement, preventing multiple private hosts from sharing the single public WAN IP.

rule_findings.fault: Dynamic NAT configuration is missing the 'overload' keyword at the end of the source mapping statement.
rule_findings.evidence: NAT inside source list statement is configured but misses the 'overload' parameter, limiting NAT to single IP mapping.
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Expected fault contains the rule's defining concepts.

results.symptom: Newly connected PCs in the training room fail to get an IP address via DHCP and fallback to APIPA addresses (169.254.x.x), while older PCs continue to work fine.
results.expected_fault: The DHCP address pool is exhausted because the configured lease range is too small (only 21 addresses) for the number of devices in the training room.

rule_findings.fault: The DHCP server address pool is exhausted because the configured lease range is too small.
rule_findings.evidence: DHCP pool show output indicates utilization mark at maximum capacity (30/30) and client fallback to APIPA.
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Expected fault contains the rule's defining concepts.

results.symptom: Network administrators can ping and manage Switch0 from the local management VLAN (VLAN 99), but pings and SSH connections from the IT office in a different subnet (VLAN 10) time out.
results.expected_fault: Switch0 is missing the 'ip default-gateway' command, preventing it from sending return traffic back to managing stations located in other subnets.

rule_findings.fault: Switch is missing the 'ip default-gateway' command, preventing management access from other subnets.
rule_findings.evidence: No 'ip default-gateway' is configured on the Layer 2 switch, and switch ping to other subnets fails.
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Expected fault contains the rule's defining concepts.

results.symptom: Wireless clients can see and associate with the guest SSID "Staff_WiFi" successfully, but they are unable to access any network resources. Checking their network status shows they did not get an IP address (status is 0.0.0.0).
results.expected_fault: The DHCP server on the wireless router's LAN interface is disabled, preventing wireless clients from acquiring IP addresses.

rule_findings.fault: The DHCP server on the wireless router's LAN interface is disabled, preventing wireless clients from acquiring IP addresses.
rule_findings.evidence: Configuration contains 'no ip dhcp server' on the wireless gateway, and client shows address 0.0.0.0.
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Expected fault contains the rule's defining concepts.

results.symptom: A new office laptop fails to connect to the corporate Wi-Fi network. The status remains "Connecting..." or fails with a security mismatch error.
results.expected_fault: Mismatched WPA2 pre-shared key (passphrase mismatch) configured on the wireless client compared to the access point's security settings.

rule_findings.fault: Mismatched WPA2 pre-shared key (passphrase mismatch) configured on the wireless client.
rule_findings.evidence: AP configuration shows wpa-psk ascii SecretPassword123, but laptop wpa-psk ascii WrongPassword123.
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Expected fault contains the rule's defining concepts.

results.symptom: The network engineer configured a standard ACL to block a host (192.168.1.10) from accessing the internet, but now all hosts in the subnet (192.168.1.0/24) are blocked from accessing the internet.
results.expected_fault: The standard ACL has a 'deny any' rule placed at the top (sequence 10), which matches all traffic and prevents the subsequent 'permit' rule from being evaluated.

rule_findings.fault: The standard ACL has a 'deny any' rule placed at the top, preventing subsequent permit rules from being evaluated.
rule_findings.evidence: ACL 10 shows 'deny any' at sequence 10 and 'permit 192.168.1.0/24' at sequence 20.
rule_findings.evaluation_reason: Expected fault contains the rule's defining concepts.
